units.en: ⟦0⟧ unlocks new infantry ⟦1⟧, motorized equipment, and mechanized equipment, as well as improving infantry and cavalry performance as a whole. It also hosts technologies that enable and improve special forces infantry, as well as an additional set of technologies enhancing special forces without ⟦2⟧.

Some of these technologies, mainly the ones affecting motorized and mechanized equipment, are interlinked with special projects, providing breakthrough progress in land warfare projects and benefitting from any ⟦0⟧ engaged in passive research in that category. Such technologies have a green ribbons in the lower right-hand corner of their icons.

Representing an infantryman's standard kit of tools and weapons, Infantry Equipment is the basis of any army. The ⟦0⟧ technology starts researched for all countries, while all major powers and many minors have the ⟦1⟧ technology researched. As infantry equipment serves as the primary, potentially only, source of stats for most unit types, unlocking and fielding upgraded versions of them earlier than the enemy can provide a significant advantage.

Later technologies also provide infantry with decent hard attack and a small amount of piercing. Although ⟦0⟧ and/or ⟦1⟧ companies, even with older equipment, will still provide infantry divisions with far more piercing, especially because 40%⟦2⟧ of a division's piercing comes from the brigade or support company with the highest amount, the additional hard attack can still make these divisions far more effective against harder opponents, like tanks or mechanized infantry.
Basic Infantry equipmentBasic infantryman equipment developed before and during the Great War.
Enables With No Step Back: Heavy Machine Gun Heavy Machine Gun Additional Machineguns
With ⟦0⟧: Heavy Machine Gun Heavy Machine Gun Additional Machineguns

Improved Infantry Equipment IPersonal and crew served weapons for infantry as well as the various other bits of kit a soldier needs. Improved weapon models and more specialized equipment.
Upgrades : Soft attack: +5% Mounted Infantry: Soft attack: +5% : Soft attack: +5%

Infantry Equipment IIPersonal and crew served weapons for infantry as well as the various other bits of kit a soldier needs. Modernized to include a great number of sub-machineguns and anti-tank rifles.
Improved Infantry Equipment IIPersonal and crew served weapons for infantry as well as the various other bits of kit a soldier needs. Improved weapon models and more specialized equipment.

Infantry Equipment IIIPersonal and crew served weapons for infantry as well as the various other bits of kit a soldier needs. Further modernized to include personal Assault Rifles and anti-tank rockets.

Improved Infantry Equipment IIIPersonal and crew served weapons for infantry as well as the various other bits of kit a soldier needs. Further Modernized to include personal Assault Rifles and anti-tank rockets. Improved availability of weapons previously distributed to a limited extent.
Upgrades : Soft attack: +5% Mounted Infantry: Soft attack: +5% : Soft attack: +10%
Infantry Anti-Tank IArming our infantry with anti-tank rifles will allow them to take out lighter armored vehicles while maintaining mobility.
Upgrades : Hard attack: +25% Piercing: +100% Mounted Infantry: Hard attack: +10% Piercing: +40%
Infantry Anti-Tank IIFor infantry to effectively engage heavier armored units, high-explosive anti-tank weapons need to be made smaller and lighter.

Support weapons includes crew-served weapons such as medium and heavy machine guns and mortars. These technologies provide bonuses to the defense and breakthrough to all types of infantry and to cavalry. This reduces incoming damage taken in combat against enemies who have greater soft and/or hard attack (dependent on the given units' hardness), though it provides little to no additional benefit against enemies with lower attack values.
Support Weapons IAutomatic weapons are becoming more portable. Submachine guns have already proven effective and the development of hand-held support weapons must continue.
Support Weapons IIThe development of automatic weapons which combine the aspects of light and heavy machine guns allows versatility in how our infantry employ their equipment.

Upgrades (Unrecognized string "Infantry Guns" for Template:Icon): Defense: +10% Soft Attack: +10% (Unrecognized string "Heavy Weapons Company" for Template:Icon): Defense: +15% Breakthrough: +15% Soft Attack: +10% (Unrecognized string "Motorized Heavy Weapons Company" for Template:Icon): Defense: +15% Breakthrough: +5% Soft Attack: +10%
Support Weapons IIIWhile maintaining and improving reliability of machine guns, we can also experiment with higher firing rates to ensure lethality of the constant stream of bullets.
Support Weapons IVWith the increased use of assault rifles, developing automatic weapons that can be used in any environment by all soldiers is a priority for a modern army.

Night vision equipment allows soldiers to see even in the dark, offsetting some of the ⟦0⟧ penalty that units receive when fighting at night, giving an edge over enemies who do not have such equipment. When combined with the ⟦1⟧ land doctrine, they can potentially remove all night fighting penalties altogether.

Night Vision IBeing able to see the enemy without being seen is key to night operations. With the invention of infra-red technology, we can outfit our army with devices which, though unwieldy, make this possible.

Night Vision IIEarly infra-red scopes, although initially intended for use by snipers, had a limited vision range. As both the portability and vision improves, these devices can be used by more troops operating at night.
Mobile Infantry technology enables ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧, as well as motorized versions of artillery brigades, motorized support companies, and other, more specialized motorized brigades.

All mobile infantry technologies are linked to land warfare special projects. They provide breakthrough progress in that category when they are being researched, and they benefit from any ⟦0⟧ engaged in passive research in that category.

Motorized versions of line brigades tend to be much faster than their non-motorized counterparts, have slightly more hardness, and be slightly better on the attack thanks to having more breakthrough, but they also tend to be more expensive, be less reliable, have more penalties on rugged terrain, and require fuel.

In addition to units, motorized technology enables and can enhance ⟦0⟧. Motorized supply extends the range of ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧, allowing them to supply units that are much further away. However, this comes at the cost of motorized equipment, both when enabling motorization and when said motorized equipment suffers losses from breakdowns in rugged ⟦3⟧ and/or bad weather and/or losses from enemy ⟦4⟧.
Early TruckDuring the Great War the armies starting using basic civilian trucks for transporting supplies and hauling equipment. These have since become an integral part of most armies
Enables With No Step Back: Wheeled Suspension

TruckMotorizing infantry is the first stage to mechanizing an army. Civilian trucks are readily adapted to military uses of transporting soldiers, towing guns, and carrying equipment and supplies. This greatly increases the strategic mobility of infantry units, which would otherwise rely on marching.

Motorized Rocket ArtilleryMultiple rocket launchers such as these deliver explosives to a target area more quickly than conventional artillery, but with lower accuracy and requiring a longer time to reload. Being mounted on trucks, this version is able to launch attacks and change positions before the enemy can return fire.

Mechanized technologies focus on improving ⟦0⟧ units and can benefit from motorized technology bonuses. Compared to ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ are slower, more expensive, and more fuel-intensive (though they are still much faster than ordinary ⟦3⟧), but they have far greater hardness and provide a lot more defense and HP. Their production costs can also be potentially through designing a variant using ⟦4⟧, which, when coupled with how few equipment losses they suffer thanks to their high HP, can actually make them more affordable in practice than ⟦5⟧ once the combat casualties start rolling in. Although their offensive stats lack compared to tanks', with enough upgrades, ⟦6⟧ can also be surprisingly capable on the offense and can even go toe-to-toe with enemy tanks when used alongside ⟦7⟧ units.

Mechanized Equipment IMechanized infantry is infantry equipped with armored personnel carriers (APCs) or infantry fighting vehicles (IFVs) for transport and combat. Mechanized infantry is distinguished from motorized infantry in that its vehicles provide a degree of protection from hostile fire, as opposed to soft-skinned wheeled vehicles (trucks or jeeps) for motorized infantry.
Upgrades Motorized, Motorized artillery, Motorized anti-air, Motorized anti-tank, Truck-Drawn Rocket Artillery: Hardness: +100% Enables With No Step Back: Half-track Suspension

Mechanized Equipment IIMechanized infantry is infantry equipped with armored personnel carriers (APCs) or infantry fighting vehicles (IFVs) for transport and combat. Mechanized infantry is distinguished from motorized infantry in that its vehicles provide a degree of protection from hostile fire, as opposed to soft-skinned wheeled vehicles (trucks or jeeps) for motorized infantry.

Mechanized Equipment IIIMechanized infantry is infantry equipped with armored personnel carriers (APCs) or infantry fighting vehicles (IFVs) for transport and combat. Mechanized infantry is distinguished from motorized infantry in that its vehicles provide a degree of protection from hostile fire, as opposed to soft-skinned wheeled vehicles (trucks or jeeps) for motorized infantry.
Upgrades Mechanized: Soft attack: +15% Hard attack: +15% Enables

⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ are special forces versions of ⟦2⟧ more suited to wet terrain and naval invasions, and as special forces, are subject to a country's special forces cap. Although they have less breakthrough than their mechanized counterparts, consume a lot more fuel, and cannot be customized using ⟦3⟧ to discount them in the same way, amtracs not only receive terrain bonuses in ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧, and ⟦6⟧ landings, but they also benefit from special forces attack bonuses from, e.g., special forces doctrines and ⟦7⟧.
These technologies can also benefit from both motorized and mechanized technology bonuses, as well as technology bonuses for naval transports.
Basic Amphibious TractorAmphibious Tractors, or Amtracs, allow Marines to be landed on a beach under armored protection. However, this comes at the cost of poor fuel efficiency.
Improved Amphibious TractorThese Amtracs feature several improvements over the base version, such as rear loading ramp for easier unloading on the beach.

⟦0⟧ and their ⟦1⟧ counterparts are avaialble with ⟦2⟧. These are effectively weaker, softer, much faster, and slightly cheaper alternatives to ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧, respectively. In theory, their niche is would be for somewhat of a hybrid role between light tanks and motorized infantry, though players may struggle to find a practical use for this niche.

With ⟦0⟧, they unfortunately suffer from being much less customizable than their tank-based counterparts. Thanks to the ⟦1⟧, once their ⟦2⟧ counterparts have become obsolete later in the game, they can get up-gunned and/or repurposed into ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, or ⟦5⟧, whereas obselete armored car upgrades are limited to incremental ⟦6⟧ where they are stuck with their outdated equipment forever. With ⟦7⟧, they further suffer from requiring their own, dedicated ⟦8⟧ that cannot be used for any other type of equipment, whereas their tank-based counterparts share their ⟦9⟧ with those that can also be used for other types of tanks, thereby offering industrial synergies that armored cars lack.
These technologies can also benefit from motorized and armor technology bonuses.
Interwar Armored CarWhere previous armored cars were simply commercial models with thin steel plating, this model was designed from the ground up to carry armor and light armament.
Basic Armored CarAn improved internal layout and additional ammunition storage creates a more effective armored car.
Improved Armored CarChanges on the battlefield require a much heavier armament and thicker armor to defeat enemy light untis and survive to report back.
Anti-Tank Armored CarOur light mechanized units will come into contact with enemy tank forces at some point. Developing a special anti-tank variant would give them a fighting chance.
